Preparing for a job interview can feel daunting, but a little planning goes a long way. Start by researching the company thoroughly. Understand its mission, products, and recent news, so you can speak knowledgeably and show genuine interest. Next, review the job description carefully and identify the key skills the employer is looking for.

Once you know what they want, think about specific examples from your experience that demonstrate those skills. The STAR method, which stands for Situation, Task, Action, and Result, is a helpful framework for structuring your answers clearly and concisely. Practice your responses out loud, either alone or with a friend, to build confidence.

It is also important to prepare thoughtful questions to ask the interviewer. This shows that you are engaged and gives you the opportunity to evaluate whether the role is the right fit for you. On the day of the interview, dress appropriately, arrive early, and bring extra copies of your resume. Above all, stay calm and be yourself. Confidence and authenticity leave a lasting impression.
